record.question:
A company hosts several HTTPS applications for unrelated domain names. Each domain already has a valid certificate, and the company must retain those certificates without reissuing them as a combined certificate. All supported clients send Server Name Indication (SNI). The company wants to serve the applications through one load balancer.

Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Attach a wildcard certificate for one of the domains and use it to authenticate all unrelated domain names.
Edit the Subject Alternative Name entries of one existing certificate to include the other domains without requesting a new certificate.
Create one CloudFront distribution and attach each existing certificate as a separate viewer certificate for that distribution.

Import the certificates into ACM as needed and add them to the HTTPS listener certificate list of an Application Load Balancer. Use SNI certificate selection and host-based listener rules for the applications.
Attach the existing certificates to a Gateway Load Balancer and configure hostname-based TLS termination.

explanation.text:
<<4>> lets one ALB HTTPS listener present different certificates for different SNI hostnames. After TLS is established, host-based listener rules can route HTTP requests to the corresponding target groups. Certificate selection and application routing are related but distinct steps.

<<1>> fails because a wildcard covers a defined domain namespace, not unrelated domains. <<2>> would invalidate the certificate’s signature; changing its covered names requires a newly issued certificate. <<3>> incorrectly assumes that one CloudFront distribution accepts multiple viewer certificates. <<5>> assigns application TLS termination and hostname routing to Gateway Load Balancer, whose purpose is transparent network appliance insertion.

Keep imported certificates renewed and ensure every certificate covers its intended hostname. A default ALB certificate handles clients without a matching SNI certificate; it does not make an unrelated hostname valid.

AWS documentation (checked 2026-09-18):
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/https-listener-certificates.html
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_ViewerCertificate.html

diagram_alt: A sequence separates certificate selection during TLS from hostname routing after TLS is established.

sources.supports: ALB certificate lists, SNI selection, wildcard scope, default certificates and renewal.
A distribution viewer certificate configuration selects one certificate.

editorial_notes: Removed irrelevant SEO framing and preserved the requirement to reuse unrelated-domain certificates.
